note: Logic gates, not prose. Each gate is: when (conditions on measured state) -> then (an ordered action chain), with the owner's own words as `why` so the reason survives. gates.py evaluates these in priority order against a state dict read off the bridge and hands the autopilot ONE chain, so the model looks up instead of re-reasoning. Lower priority number fires first. The gates are a PLC ladder: measured inputs, rungs scanned by priority, the highest live rung wins, and a rung can only be reached when the rungs below it hold -- survive, then power, then defence, then production, then the mountain, then off-world.

tags.note: PLC tag table. CONSTANTS are safety limits and never auto-change. VARIABLES are setpoints that scale with the empire -- gates.py recomputes them from measured state each scan and writes them back, so one colony of three and an empire of thirty read the same ladder with different numbers. Reference them in a gate's `when` as {NAME}.

BEDS_NEEDED.rule: one per colonist, plus one spare

COOLERS_PER_ROOM.rule: one per room up to 3 rooms, then one per 2 rooms
